newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B share index ends down on Lujiazui.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B share index ends down on Lujiazui.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended slightly down on Wednesday mainly due to a fall in real estate developer Lujiazui, traders said.
Trading was dull and dominated by local retail investors, with foreign investors taking a Christmas holiday, they said.
The index fell 0.289 points or 0.45 percent to 64.299, on thin volume of 7.7 million shares worth $3.5 million.

Traders said investors sold Lujiazui because it would list on Thursday an additional 60 million B shares. These shares were sold earlier this month in a three-for-10 rights issue, which diluted the value of other shares, they said.
Lujiazui was the most active stock, falling $0.020 or 1.60 percent to $1.226, on volume of 1.3 million shares.
"Trading was quiet, with the market in a holiday mood," said one trader. "A rebound on the A share market sparked a little individual buying late on, which trimmed early losses."
"With overseas investors taking a holiday, the market is expected to move in a narrow range in the next few days," a second trader said.
Out of 42 B shares, 41 traded, with 21 down, 11 flat and nine up.
P & T Equipment was the biggest loser on small liquidation selling, down $0.026 or 6.07 percent to $0.402, on volume of 82,000 shares.

Shanghai's A share index had a technical rebound after sharp losses in the past few days, partly because the exchange denied rumours that it would replace the current next-day settlement with a three-day settlement system.
The index jumped 32.006 or 3.55 percent to 932.773 points on volume of 389.4 million shares worth 3.3 billion yuan.
The SSE 30 blue-chip index closed up 65.376 points or 2.78 percent to 2419.739 points.
